criteria.criterion: A new driver test in crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs shows a child ending with no result while the kill switch is on yields InvocationOutcome::Killed with a detail naming the kill switch, not Error. Run: cargo test -p athena-agent.
criteria.evidence: I ran the new test a_child_ending_without_a_result_while_the_kill_switch_is_on_is_killed_not_an_error and it passed. In the test, a stand-in child writes the stop file and exits with code 143 before the driver's once-a-second poll, which is the race the review describes. The test asserts Killed and a detail containing "kill switch". It then runs the same early exit with the switch off and asserts Error. The fix in claude.rs (lines 396-401) checks registry.stopped() after the child exits with no result.

criteria.criterion: A new scoring test in crates/athena-score builds a job whose execution cost is only a bound and shows the cost_usd quantity score is provisional; a job with exact costs is not provisional. Run: cargo test -p athena-score.
criteria.evidence: 12 tests passed, including a_cost_known_only_as_a_bound_scores_provisional_and_a_firm_cost_does_not. With costs firm plus bound, cost_usd is provisional and wall_time_s is not. With two firm costs, cost_usd is not provisional. a_provisional_quantity_does_not_count_in_aggregates also passed.

criteria.criterion: An end-to-end test in crates/athena-cli/tests/lifecycle.rs shows a producer stopped by the kill switch closes with a killed invocation record and a provisional cost score, and the commit gate accepts the recomputed score. Run: cargo test -p athena-cli.
criteria.evidence: a_producer_stopped_by_the_kill_switch_closes_killed_with_a_provisional_cost_score passed, and so did every athena-cli test (44 in lifecycle.rs). The test asserts that the committed 02-producer.json is Killed with a kill-switch detail and cost value None, that score.json has cost_usd provisional and wall_time_s not, and that check_history() reports no violations. The fake driver is scripted to return Killed, so this test checks how records and scores handle a kill. The driver's own attribution is covered by criterion 1.

criteria.criterion: Whole workspace passes cargo test and cargo clippy --all-targets with no warnings; cargo fmt --check is clean.
criteria.evidence: fmt printed nothing. clippy finished with no warnings; it reused cached build output from Athena's earlier run. Athena reports that cargo test --locked passed with 852 tests. I also ran the agent, score and cli crates myself and all passed.

criteria.criterion: A bound-only cost is no longer scored as a firm figure, and a provisional cost_usd score does not count in aggregates as a resolved value.
criteria.evidence: Read the change. score_records sets cost_provisional from cost_is_only_a_bound (any execution cost whose value() is None), and the flag is written into the QuantityScore. aggregate() skips provisional quantities. athena-core scoring::history drops provisional cost_usd, so the reference forecast does not learn from it. One gap: the score line in display.rs still prints "cost WIS" with no provisional marker (see findings).

criteria.criterion: Older score.json records without the new field still deserialize (serde default); existing history tests still pass.
criteria.evidence: The new field is declared with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")]. The new test a_quantity_score_written_before_the_provisional_field_still_reads parses JSON without the field, and athena-data's tests passed in Athena's full run. Existing lifecycle and history tests passed in my cargo test -p athena-cli run.

criteria.criterion: docs/records.md describes the provisional quantity field and kill-switch attribution, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry citing m8 of docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-acceptance-1.md.
criteria.evidence: docs/records.md has two new paragraphs: one says a kill-switch stop is recorded as killed even when the child died between the driver's checks, and one covers the provisional field (its meaning, excluded from aggregates and history, omitted when false, older records read as false). Both match the code. CHANGELOG.md gains an entry under Changed that cites m8 of docs/design/reviews/athena-v0-acceptance-1.md.

findings.summary: Two changed files are not on the expected deliverables list, and one listed file (athena-core/src/lib.rs) was not changed.
findings.evidence: The diffstat shows changes to crates/athena-core/src/scoring.rs and crates/athena-data/src/records.rs. The list names crates/athena-core/src/lib.rs. Both edits are needed for the fix: the QuantityScore field lives in athena-data, and the history filter lives in scoring.rs. The reading said the exact paths were inferred.

findings.summary: The status score line still shows a provisional cost's interval score as if it were firm.
findings.evidence: The loop over score.quantities prints "cost WIS {:.2}" for every quantity and ignores q.provisional. In the m8 case a maintainer would still see, for example, "cost WIS 4.02" with nothing saying it is only a bound.

findings.summary: Part of m8 is not covered: the job's reason mentioning the kill switch.
findings.evidence: m8 also says "the job's reason does not mention the kill switch". The accepted reading leaves this out, and the new end-to-end test checks only the invocation detail, not the outcome's reason.

summary: The change fixes both parts of m8 at their source. First, after the agent's process exits without a result, the driver now checks whether the kill switch is on and, if so, records the invocation as `killed`. This closes the gap where `athena stop` ended the process between two of the driver's once-a-second checks. Second, the scorer marks `cost_usd` as `provisional` when any execution cost is only a bound. Provisional costs are left out of aggregates and out of the history the reference forecast learns from. Older `score.json` files still load, because the new field defaults to false when it is missing. I ran the agent, score and full cli test suites, fmt and clippy, and all passed. The new tests show killed against error with the switch on and off, provisional against firm costs, aggregates leaving the provisional cost out, and the commit gate accepting the recomputed score. Three minor findings: two needed files are outside the deliverables list; the status line still prints a provisional cost's interval score with no marker; and the review's remark that the job's reason does not mention the kill switch is not covered.
